title: Sebastian and the Summit
premise: Isandro Vane, a railroad engineer who keeps a map of closed lines and never stays anywhere long enough to be found, is hired to trace a vanished government survey team in the Kestrel Range. Following the team's abandoned gear and the impossible absence of tracks, Isandro discovers the survey was hunting an old private railway fortune buried in a summit tunnel—and that the Vane family name is written into its deeds. Hunted by the syndicate that erased the surveyors, Isandro must cross the range ahead of the snows with two unlikely companions, choosing at last between disappearing forever and claiming an inheritance that would end their running. They reach the tunnel as winter closes, expose the syndicate's claim, and for the first time stop moving—because staying has finally cost less than leaving.
about_author: Marguerite Yarrow is a former land surveyor who spent six years mapping decommissioned rail lines across the northern ranges before turning to fiction. She writes from a cabin with no road access, which she insists is a professional preference rather than an escape.

chapters.title: The Map of Closed Lines
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. In a rail-town hotel, Isandro works by lamplight on a hand-drawn map of shuttered lines, establishing their ritual of never unpacking fully. A telegram arrives offering dangerous money to find a missing survey team. Beat: restless competence shadowed by loneliness.

chapters.title: Money That Doesn't Ask Questions
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The client, a lawyer named Corvus Hale, pays too well and asks too little; Isandro takes the job anyway because winter money is survival money. A brief flashback shows why stopping costs more. Beat: wary bargain struck against better judgment.

chapters.title: Gear Without Ghosts
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, joined by tracker Odile Ferran. At the survey's last camp they find tents pitched, instruments calibrated, food untouched—abandoned mid-task, no tracks leading out. Odile reads the snow like text and finds nothing, which is worse than anything. Beat: first true dread.

chapters.title: The Surveyor's Notebook
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Among the gear, Odile finds a field notebook whose final pages are torn out, the stubs matching a page hidden in Isandro's own map case—someone slipped it there before they left town. Beat: paranoia ignites; the hunt has already begun.

chapters.title: Company on the Switchback
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Climbing into the foothills, they catch a stowaway: Tam, a teenage runaway who stole onto their supply sled. Turning back means days lost; bringing Tam means responsibility. Beat: reluctant warmth cracking Isandro's armor.

chapters.title: What the Torn Pages Said
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam deciphers the recovered page: coordinates for a summit tunnel and the word VANE repeated in the margins. Isandro goes white and says nothing. Beat: the past surfaces; inheritance becomes threat instead of gift.

chapters.title: Men Who Move Like Weather
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Riders appear on the lower slopes, methodical, sweeping the mountain in a grid—the syndicate's recovery crew, erasing evidence. The trio cuts their camp and moves at night. Beat: pursuit begins; the mountain turns hostile.

chapters.title: The Bridge at Coldwater Gorge
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. To gain a day, Isandro leads them across a rotten trestle from the closed-line map, engineering knowledge pitted against decay. The bridge half-fails behind them. Beat: expertise vindicated, nerves shredded.

chapters.title: Snowline
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. First snow falls early. Tam, freezing and scared, demands answers; Isandro finally admits the Vanes built the summit line and were ruined for it—that Isandro has been running from the name ever since. Beat: confession; the trio becomes a unit.

chapters.title: The Hermit of the High Pasture
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. They shelter with Anselm, an old line-keeper living illegally in a maintenance hut, who recognizes the Vane name and reveals the syndicate didn't just ruin the Vanes—it murdered them over the tunnel's mineral rights. Beat: grief transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Anselm's Ledger
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Anselm produces decades of records proving the syndicate falsified the closure surveys. But riders reach the pasture; Anselm stays behind to burn his hut as cover. Beat: sacrifice; the cost of standing still made visible.

chapters.title: Running the Scree
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. A desperate descent-and-climb through loose rock as the recovery crew closes in. Tam freezes on a ledge; Odile talks them across. Beat: fear mastered; Tam earns their place.

chapters.title: The Tunnel Mouth
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. They reach the sealed summit tunnel and breach it with survey charges. Inside: intact track, ore cars, and the bones of the last Vane crew—who weren't fleeing. They were walled in. Beat: horror; the inheritance revealed as massacre site.

chapters.title: What Was Buried
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Deep in the tunnel, the torn notebook pages' author—a surveyor who survived long enough to write—is found with documents naming every syndicate partner. The storm arrives outside, sealing them in. Beat: triumph curdled by entrapment.

chapters.title: Trapped With the Truth
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Snowbound, supplies failing, the trio debates: destroy the documents and vanish, or carry them down and face Hale and the syndicate. Isandro chooses, for once, not to run. Beat: the thematic hinge—staying chosen freely.

chapters.title: Hale at the Door
chapters.summary: Hale's POV (brief). Hale arrives at the tunnel mouth with the recovery crew, offering Isandro partnership and a new name in exchange for the documents. He genuinely believes everyone can be bought. Beat: temptation articulated; corruption wears a reasonable face.

chapters.title: The Price of a Name
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro stalls Hale inside the dark tunnel while Odile and Tam rig the old ore cars and charge lines. The negotiation becomes a duel of stories: what power is for. Beat: moral climax approaching; Isandro refuses the deal.

chapters.title: Collapse
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The planned collapse goes wrong; Odile is caught in the fall sealing the syndicate crew inside the deep workings. Tam and Isandro dig through the night. Beat: climax and devastating loss.

chapters.title: What Odile Left
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Odile survives, barely, but her tracking days are done; she gives Isandro her father's compass and tells them to finish it. The syndicate's local men, leaderless and exposed by the documents, scatter. Beat: mourning and resolve entwined.

chapters.title: Descent Before Thaw
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The three descend the mountain carrying the truth, pursued now by weather alone. Tam, who ran away from a home, realizes Isandro is running toward one. Beat: quiet grace after violence.

chapters.title: The Hearing at Grayfall Junction
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. In a packed rail-town hall, Isandro presents the ledger, the pages, and the map of closed lines—every lie redrawn as evidence. The syndicate's claims dissolve; the Vane deed stands. Beat: public reckoning; power answered with record.

chapters.title: Stopping
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, closing with Tam's. Spring. Isandro signs the restoration order for the summit line, unpacks completely for the first time in the book, and hangs the map on a wall instead of carrying it. Beat: belonging achieved; the journey ends where staying begins.
